articles.title: I kept wishing there was an “iLovePDF for text” - so I started building one
articles.excerpt: I use websites like iLovePDF, Smallpdf, Canva, and iLoveIMG quite often. They make it really easy when I need to do something with a PDF or an image. But I noticed something while working with plain t…
articles.body: I use websites like iLovePDF, Smallpdf, Canva, and iLoveIMG quite often. They make it really easy when I need to do something with a PDF or an image. But I noticed something while working with plain text. There wasn't really a place that felt like that for everyday text work. Whenever I needed to do something with text, I'd end up searching Google, opening a random website, doing the task, and moving on. Then I'd have to do the same thing again a few days later. That honestly got a little annoying. So I decided to try building my own version of that idea, but specifically for text. I called it iLoveText. https://ilovetext.online It's still a work in progress, and I'm adding things as I use them myself.

articles.title: “Software Engineering is dead”
articles.excerpt: Every time a new AI model is released — especially after Fable and now with GPT-Astra — everyone exclaims, ‘Software engineering is dead’. I decided to write this after watching a well-known data scie…
articles.body: Every time a new AI model is released — especially after Fable and now with GPT-Astra — everyone exclaims, ‘Software engineering is dead’. I decided to write this after watching a well-known data scientist who, without offering any justification, utters that phrase yet again. The only “proof of authority” for this claim is: “I sit down at the table with executives from Microsoft, Google, and other companies that have built software products without writing a single line of code”. I believe this statement is completely wrong , and I’ll first give you some technical reasons, followed by an anthropological explanation as to why this phrase is repeated periodically. Technical reason #1: Software engineering is not only about code.

articles.body: Most RAG tutorials start by installing a vector database. For a lot of projects, that is a dependency you don't need yet. I measured how long plain exact search takes as the corpus grows, and what an HNSW index buys you in return. Short answer: below about 100,000 chunks, a numpy matrix multiply is fast enough for almost any RAG app. Between 100k and 1M it depends on your traffic. Past that, use an index. articles.title: Showing EngineHP and Displacement from vPIC Without Implying Dyno Numbers
articles.excerpt: NHTSA vPIC often returns engine-shaped fields: horsepower-ish values, displacement in liters or cubic centimeters, cylinder counts, fuel type. Product teams love putting a big "280 HP" badge on the de…
articles.body: NHTSA vPIC often returns engine-shaped fields: horsepower-ish values, displacement in liters or cubic centimeters, cylinder counts, fuel type. Product teams love putting a big "280 HP" badge on the decode card. Buyers love it too -- until they treat that badge like a dyno sheet from last Saturday. This post is about honest display: surface EngineHP and displacement when vPIC provides them, label the source, and refuse to imply measured crank or wheel horsepower. What vPIC is (and is not) saying DecodeVinValues-style payloads may include fields such as EngineHP , DisplacementL , DisplacementCC , EngineCylinders , and fuel-related attributes. These are catalog / manufacturer-reported characteristics associated with the VIN decode, not a live measurement of the vehicle in front of you.

articles.title: How Angular Signals Work Under the Hood: Reactive Primitives and Change Detection
articles.excerpt: Ever had a component in Angular that stubbornly refuses to update when you think it should? You tweak some state, and the UI looks frozen , no error, no warning, just silence. Then, after some trial a…
articles.body: Ever had a component in Angular that stubbornly refuses to update when you think it should? You tweak some state, and the UI looks frozen , no error, no warning, just silence. Then, after some trial and error, you realize the problem isn’t your code but how Angular’s new Signals system tracks dependencies and triggers change detection. I hit this wall recently while migrating a complex form to use Angular Signals. At first glance, signals seemed like magic , reactive primitives that promised simpler state management and automatic updates. But the behavior wasn’t always intuitive, especially when combined with Angular’s existing change detection mechanism.

articles.title: 6 Years Later, Netflix's Chilling Sleeper Hit Series Is About to Disappear From Streaming
articles.excerpt: Catch Deadwind, a chilling Finnish crime drama, before it leaves Netflix later this month.
articles.body: Few things in television possess the intoxicating gravity of a masterfully crafted mystery series. The Killing expands a single tragedy into a sprawling multiple-season-long portrait of grief and political corruption, while Mare of Easttown scrapes back the veneer of a small-town homicide to expose the generational wounds festering beneath. Such greats as The Outsider and, more recently, Lanterns subvert the genre entirely by anchoring their investigations in procedural grit before letting supernatural elements bleed into the frame. The finest of these shows care far less about the mechanical puzzle of who committed the crime than the psychological debris left in its wake.

articles.body: 2 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Artist’s rendering of the lunar South Pole region. Glowing points of light scattered across the lunar surface represent surface assets supporting sustained human and robotic operations near the South Pole. NASA As an astronaut traverses the lunar South Pole, tribocharging from walking on the lunar surface and plasma charging from the ambient plasma generate electric charge on the spacesuit. This problem is severely compounded when entering lunar shadows and Permanently Shadowed Regions (PSRs). In these dark zones, the spacesuit can buildup a substantial negative potential due to a lack of ambient ion flux and the absence of photoelectron emission to balance ambient electron collection.
